The '''Saochian Reorganization Period''' was a mid-nineteenth-century crisis and reform period in Saochi/Saochai, lasting approximately from 1841 to 1863 in old source material.

== Background ==

The period was marked by famine, fractured governance, urban discontent, and the weakening of older agrarian traditions. These pressures created an intellectual opening for new reform philosophies, including [[Kaonism]].

== Kaonist Development ==

[[Liao Zhengyuan]] formulated Kaonism during this period. His writings framed social disorder as a failure of rhythm between law, labor, nature, and moral authority.

The period ended before Kaonism could become a mass movement. Two years later, the [[Purge of 1865]] suppressed Kaonist circles and other alternative reform schools.
